Items.Authors: Michael J. Freyberg, Norbert Meidinger, Michael Smith, Emanuele Perinati
Items.Title: Long-term evolution of micrometeoroid impact effects in pnCCDs (EPIC-pn, eROSITA)
Items.Abstract: Impacts of micro-meteoroids as micron-sized dust particles at hypervelocities onto X-ray astromonmical CCDs in space can cause performance degradation but also lead to fatal failures.  Here we report on the 3 impacts onto the pn-CCDs of XMM-Newton (EPIC-pn camera) and the 7 onto eROSITA aboard Spectum-Roentgen-Gamma.  We analyze in detail the long-term evolution of the damage effects in these back-illuminated silicon devices.  We discuss the presence and absence of associated optical flashes.

Items.Authors: Jianan Cong, Zhengyang Li, Xiaoyan Li
Items.Title: System design of the wide-field near-infrared telescope at Dome A, Antarctica, and first daytime near-infrared observations
Items.Abstract: Dome A in Antarctica likely has the best observing conditions on the Earth's surface in the near-infrared owing to its sky-light background and superior seeing conditions. This work introduces the system design of the first wide field-of-view near-infrared telescope at Dome A. We present the telescope’s optical system as well as the design of the direct-drive motor mount and mechanical defrosting system capable of withstanding the extreme Antarctic environment. Through this project, we validated the key technologies described above and achieved the first daytime J-band bright-star observations during the Antarctic summer. Stars as faint as J- 10.06 mag were significantly detected with an effective exposure time of 175 s around midnight.

Items.Authors: James H. Tutt, Bruce Lairson, Jeffrey De Lucca, Alexandra Higley, Ross McCurdy, Randall L. McEntaffer, Drew M. Miles, Keith Rice
Items.Title: Testing of SiC grid-based blocking filters to increase their technology readiness level
Items.Abstract: Progress over the past year has advanced mitigation of contamination buildup on cold focal-plane detectors using free-standing, actively heated blocking filters. Development, fabrication, and environmental testing of large-format SiC support grids have continued, enabling room-temperature X-ray filters with minimal power. Multiple square-grid designs suitable for the AXIS mission have been produced and mechanically tested, including vibration evaluations for launch survivability. Thermal-vacuum experiments have mapped steady-state and transient temperature behavior, refining power-budget models for reheating under radiative cooling. Next steps include additional vibration tests, long-duration thermal-vacuum cycles, and studies of filter thermal conductivity to further raise TRL. These results position SiC room-temperature blocking filters as a strong solution for future missions requiring contamination control and thermal efficiency.

Items.Authors: Jessica A. Gaskin, Julie A. Crooke
Items.Title: The ASTRA Initiative: Preparing for future NASA large strategic astrophysics missions
Items.Abstract: This presentation summarizes he Astrophysics Strategic Technology & Research Accelerator (ASTRA) Initiative and discusses, NASA’s progress in executing the Astro2020 Decadal Survey recommendations, and outlines the strategic steps being undertaken to prepare for future strategic astrophysics missions. Support for the community considers previous efforts – including existing concept studies developed for Astro2020, the current global astronomical environment of existing and planned missions, increased industry capability, and technological advances/investments over the past decade. The discussion will highlight the interplay of technological advancements and mission planning essential for future exploration in astrophysics and astronomy and will emphasize the value and criticality of industry and international partnering.

Items.Authors: Janus D. Brink, J. Christopher Clemens, Kieran Leschinski
Items.Title: Pathfinder curved grating spectrometer for the ELT
Items.Abstract: With the Vera C. Rubin observatory on the brink of delivering a flood of transient alerts to the time-domain astronomy community, the need for efficient spectroscopic follow-up is now more critical than ever. We present a compact, high-efficiency curved grating spectrometer design with broad visible band coverage aimed at efficient spectroscopic follow-up. Our pathfinder instrument design is matched to the University of Vienna’s 1.5 m Figl telescope. We describe the spectrometer’s characteristics and expected performance in this configuration and also illustrate the feasibility of extending the design for operation as a visitor instrument of the European Large Telescope.

Items.Authors: Myriam Rodrigues, Alondra Solá, Clément Hottier, Hermine Schnetler, Raziye Artan, Nazim A. Bharmal, Diane Chapuis, Gavin Dalton, Michel Dupieux, Kacem El Hadi, Marc Jaquet, Andreas Kelz, Marie Larrieu, Laurent Martin, Meghna Mohamed, Timothy J. Morris, Ana Perez, Eric Prieto, Jay Stephen, Roser Pello, Mathieu Puech, Thomas Augusteijn, María Luisa García-Vargas, Alessandro Meoli, Ruben Sanchez-Janssen, Christian Surace, Franck Ducret
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: building a comprehensive engineering database
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, the multi-object spectrograph for the ESO Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), is developed by a dis-  tributed consortium involving multiple institutes and engineering disciplines. Maintaining consistency between  requirements, interfaces, product definitions, verification activities and engineering documentation is therefore a  major systems engineering challenge. To address this, the project implemented a central engineering information  model using ReqSuite® Requirement Management tool. Rather than limiting the repository to requirements  management, the database also stores other engineering artifacts, such as Product Breakdown Structure, inter-  faces, configuration items and verification information, providing a common technical reference for the project.  Behavioural and parametric models -such as observing sequences, funcional analysis and performances calculator-  remain in their specialised engineering tools but are connected to the database through traceability links and  applic

Items.Authors: Angiola Orlando
Items.Title: The Simons Observatory: two new Small Aperture Telescopes employing feedhorn-coupled OMT dichroic Kinetic Inductance Detectors
Items.Abstract: The Simons Observatory (SO) is a ground-based cosmic microwave background (CMB) survey experiment consisting of three 0.5m small-aperture telescopes (SATs) and one 6m large-aperture telescope (LAT), observing from an altitude of 5200m in the Atacama Desert in Chile. These instruments employ over 120000 superconducting transition edge sensor (TES) detectors operating at frequency bands between 30GHz and 280GHz and are conducting regular observations for a broad range of CMB science goals, including searches for primordial gravitational waves through B-mode polarization. We are planning to deploy two additional SATs employing arrays of dual-polarization feedhorn-coupled multichroic Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs) operating at 90/150GHz and bespoke warm detector readout electronics.The integration and testing of both SAT receivers are underway in the UK. We provide an overview of these receivers, discuss integration status and achieved performance on the path to deployment.

Items.Authors: Dinko Milaković, Guido Cupani, Bruce Bassett, Stefano Cristiani, Luca Pasquini
Items.Title: "Perfect" spectra for ESO’s HARPS spectrograph
Items.Abstract: Harperfect is the first application of spectral perfectionism to a high-resolution echelle spectrograph, recon-  structing 1D spectra from 2D detector data via a forward model built on a calibration matrix of PSF shape,  wavelength, and order trace, built entirely from laser frequency comb (LFC) observations. HARPS cannot re-  solve individual LFC lines, so each of 21 148 identified lines directly samples the PSF. We modelled these with  a bivariate Gaussian, determining the PSF anywhere on the detector, calibrating wavelength, and tracing or-  ders more accurately than the standard HARPS pipeline. Applied to 52.5 hours of HARPS data on quasar  HE0515−4414, Harperfect gives S/N comparable to, though slightly lower than, the standard pipeline. Its  value lies in an exact resolution matrix and independent samples, properties standard extraction cannot guar-  antee for a non-separable PSF – a step toward better measurements of fundamental constants and exoplanet  atmospheres.

Items.Authors: Olivier Corpace, Jean-Christophe Barrière, Patrice Charon, Jean Fontigniè, Stéphane Jurie, Mickaël Lacroix, Yannick Le Noa, Philippe Le Pouhalec, François Puel
Items.Title: 14 indexed cryogenic mechanisms for ELT-METIS, a challenging MAIT phase
Items.Abstract: This paper describes the work performed by the CEA Paris-Saclay team during six years to produce 14 indexed cryogenic mechanisms (ICAR) for ELT-METIS. These actuators operate at 40 K and achieve the positioning of optical elements in the METIS infrared instrument within a few arcseconds precision. The production of this small series was punctuated by a number of commercial and technical challenges. This article deals with the procurement strategy, the manufacturing pitfalls, the assembly optimization and the test facility adaptation.

Items.Authors: Andrey M. Baryshev, Carlos de Breuck, Tinus Stander, Katherine Cortés Urbina, Pamela Pizarro, Ot Roof, Ronald Hesper
Items.Title: A comparison of approaches to interferometric atmospheric turbulence measurements at proposed AtLAST sites
Items.Abstract: The Atacama Large Aperture Submillimeter Telescope (AtLAST) project is currently comparing atmospheric turbulence at two candidate sites on the Chajnantor plain. We report on the comparison of two atmospheric interferometers on site, both using Ku-band geostationary satellite beacons. The reference instrument uses a common local source for downconversion, while the experimental instrument correlates offline data from two independent receivers, relying on short-term phase coherence. While the former approach produces lower phase error and improved resolution, the latter does not require cabling or trenching on site, which is a significant advantage in deployment.

Items.Authors: Patricio Galeas, Rodrigo Seguel, Sebastian Carrasco, Rodrigo Augsburger, Fernando Huenupan, Ania Cravero, Jaime Guarda, Angel Otárola, Florian Kerber, Tzu-Chiang Shen
Items.Title: A drone-based atmospheric monitoring system for astronomical observatories
Items.Abstract: The ABL-Drone project addresses the need for high-resolution measurements of the Atmospheric Boundary Layer (ABL), a key region that influences meteorological phenomena and optical turbulence, directly affecting astronomical observations.    This study reports on the development, integration, and field testing of a drone-based monitoring platform of the ABL equipped with fast response and accurate sensors for the monitoring of the vertical profiles of barometric pressure, air temperature and humidity, as well as the horizontal wind speed. This setup, together with an optimal operational procedure, produces data useful to derive the strength of the optical turbulence, Cn2(z) profile, with a controllable vertical resolution in the range of a few tens of meters.    The initial prototype was successfully validated at ESO’s Paranal Observatory, demonstrating strong potential to complement or replace traditional instruments by automated drone flights during the night.

Items.Authors: Steven R. Gibson
Items.Title: A few systems-engineering tools
Items.Abstract: Described here are a few systems-engineering and documentation tools that have proven useful during the development of two astronomical instruments. They are particularly helpful for developing the systems-level view of the electronic and software needs of the instrument. The end results become useful references, and the making of the diagrams and tools is extremely helpful as the process inherently finds gaps in the design. The tools discussed include timeline diagrams, wiki pages, electronics spreadsheets, and connection diagrams. Timeline diagrams illuminate the sequences and interactions between observers, software, and subsystems. Wiki pages are used to collect together subsystem and device details. An electronics spreadsheet informs on power draw, heat generation, rack space use and other items. And finally, connection diagrams illustrate how the various electronic components connect together and interact with each other.

Items.Authors: Hemanth Manikantan, Carlo Lefevre, Lorenzo Petrucci, Paolo Soffitta, Fabio Muleri, Enrico Costa, Alda Rubini, Vladislavs Plesanovs, Markus Gruber, Jochen Kaminski, Klaus Desch, Alessandro Di Marco, Sergio Fabiani, Riccardo Ferrazzoli, Saba Imtiaz, Dawoon Kim, Alessandro Lacerenza, John Rankin, Ajay Ratheesh
Items.Title: A focal-plane x-ray polarimeter with spectral and timing capabilities for future missions
Items.Abstract: Future X-ray missions require focal-plane detectors capable of performing high-sensitivity polarimetry without compromising timing or spectroscopy. We present a new photoelectron-track X-ray polarimeter built on IXPE and GridPix heritage. The prototype features a photon-absorption and drift region with a uniform electric field shaped by equally spaced metallic rings to preserve track morphology. The design supports interchangeable drift lengths, operation in 1–3 atm pressure, and compatibility with a gas-mixing system for three-component mixtures. Charge amplification and readout are provided by an InGrid Micromegas on a Timepix3 ASIC. The 256×256 pixels and 1.5625 ns time resolution of Timepix3 enable full 3D track reconstruction, while <1 μs deadtime allows operation at high count rates. We present detector construction, characterization, and first results from polarized X-ray measurements.

Items.Authors: Dan Jarvis, Vik S. Dhillon, Martin J. Dyer, Joe Lyman, Stu Littlefair, Kendall Ackley, Sergey Belkin, Lisa Kelsey, Tom Killestein, Amit Kumar, David O'Neill, Krzysztof Ulaczyk, Danny Steeghs, Duncan K. Galloway, Paul O'Brien, Gavin Ramsay, Kanthanakorn Noysena, Rubina Kotak, Rene Breton, Laura Nuttall, Ben Gompertz, Jorge Casares Velázquez, Don Pollacco
Items.Title: A forced photometry service for the Gravitational-wave Optical Transient Observer (GOTO)
Items.Abstract: The Gravitational-wave Optical Transient Observer (GOTO) is a robotic array of 32 wide-field telescopes split between twin antipodal sites. Project aims include rapid optical follow-up of gravitational-wave detections, and transient detection from 3-day-cadence all-sky surveys in the wide L-band filter (~400-700 nm).    GOTO Lightcurve is a forced photometry service providing an API and web interface to query 3 years worth of sky survey products from the GOTO pipeline. The Lightcurve back-end optimises I/O by caching extraction counts and alternate calibration post-processing, enabling the API to provide daily lightcurve updates at a rate of ~10 targets per second to internal systems.    When comparing between the 32 telescopes, variations in throughput and relative colour response are evident. A baseline colour response model has been constructed to apply L-band colour corrections for targets with known colour to fix this issue, and track ongoing changes to colour sensitivity.

Items.Authors: Alberto Hernández Fernández, David Díaz Martín, José Javier Díaz García, Roger John Hoyland, Luis Fernando Rodríguez Ramos, Diego Portero Rodríguez, Silvestre Rodríguez Pérez
Items.Title: A high-isolation wideband channelizer for MKID readouts: a custom HLS implementation on RFSoC
Items.Abstract: We present a high-performance channelizer for Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors (MKIDs), designed to mitigate spectral leakage and scalloping loss via a 50% overlapping Polyphase Filter Bank (PFB). Implemented on a Xilinx Zynq UltraScale+ RFSoC, our custom Vitis HLS design processes a 4.096 GSps input using a Super Sample Rate (SSR) of 32. Unlike prior art relying on aggressive 512 MHz clocking and standard IPs, our novel split-path architecture (delayed/non-delayed branches) operates at a robust 256 MHz, enabling a deep 16-tap prototype filter that doubles the channel isolation of comparable systems. Validated cryogenically with an MKID array in an Adiabatic Demagnetization Refrigerator (ADR), the system delivers a flat spectral response across 2 MHz channels, establishing a new benchmark for resource-efficient, wideband FDM readouts.

Items.Authors: Ruirui Fan, Xiaoyun Ma, Xiaohui Yan, Xiaojing Wu, Wei Wang, Nannan Yue, Xiangxiang Ren, Yu Wang, Yuxin Qiu, Hanzhang Wang, Fei Liu, Ran Duan
Items.Title: A high-speed readout system for TES/MKID arrays
Items.Abstract: This work presents a universal high-speed readout system for large-scale frequency-division multiplexed superconducting detector arrays, such as MKIDs and TESs. Utilizing a heterogeneous FPGA-GPU architecture, the system operates in the 4-8 GHz range with a 2 GHz bandwidth, enabling simultaneous readout of 2000 frequency channels in one module of the system at a data rate of 31.25 kHz. It introduces three automated operational modes—Network Analyzer Mode, Detector Driving Optimization Mode, and Formal Observation Mode—to streamline resonator characterization, driving frequency and power tuning, and real-time data acquisition. Performance results demonstrate the system as an efficient solution for large-scale detector arrays in astrophysics and other applications.

Items.Authors: Sofia Dimoudi, David Barr, John Connolly, Meryem K. Dag, Thomas N. Davies, Deli Geng, James P. Gill-Fleming, Aurelie Magniez, Kieran S. O'Brien
Items.Title: A hybrid FPGA-GPU readout system for MKID detectors in astronomy: End-to-end data validation and performance.
Items.Abstract: Current readout systems for MKIDs (Microwave Kinetic Inductance Detectors) with FPGA-based architectures tend to be limited by cost per feedline, with respect to array size and processing sophistication that can be achieved. To address these challenges, a hybrid readout system for MKIDs is currently being built at Durham University that combines the low latency – high throughput capabilities of the current RFSoC technology with the parallel computational power of GPUs . The system consists of the RFSoC 4x2 board that manages the real-time probing and acquisition of the detector signal, alongside channelisation and network transmission, a high-speed interface transferring network packets directly to the on-board memory of one or more NVIDIA GPUs, and discrete GPU(s) processing phase data to extract photon information in real time. We present results from end-to-end experiments, using this readout configuration with 1000 resonators per feedline, scaling to multiple feedlines.

Items.Authors: Tongyu Mao, Shibo Shu, Congzhan Liu
Items.Title: A KIDs array readout system based on RFSoC and PYNQ using high-level synthesis
Items.Abstract: We present a HDL-Free readout system for a kinetic inductance detectors (KIDs) array based on the ANTSDR T510 RFSoC design board and PYNQ, utilizing High-Level Synthesis (HLS) and Xilinx official IP cores without the need for custom Verilog or VHDL code. The system consists of several key components: signal generation, frequency mixing, PFB channelization, channel remapping, DDC processing, timestamping, DMA packaging, and UDP transmission. Each part can be easily controlled on the PYNQ platform through Jupyter Notebook. The system allows for a simple switch between the 512 MHz and 2048 MHz bandwidth versions by modifying a few parameters in the block design and C++ code. This system reduces the deployment threshold and customization costs, provides a high-bandwidth, low-cost, and scalable platform for large-scale KIDs array readout, and features a modular design for easy component reuse.

Items.Authors: Pedro Pablo Silva, Gaspar Fabrega, Vicente Lizana, Ingeborg Muñoz, Juan Pablo Gil, Eduardo Peña
Items.Title: A KRaft-mode Kafka middleware architecture for operational data analysis at Paranal Observatory
Items.Abstract: The Paranal Observatory produces heterogeneous operational data streams-software logs, numerical telemetry, monitoring metrics, and status events-that are essential for troubleshooting, monitoring, and engineering decision-making. This paper presents a hybrid streaming middleware architecture that places Apache Kafka downstream of DLABMON, the existing collection and parsing layer. The architecture is designed around separation of concerns, replayable streams, consumer independence, and replicated storage. The implementation uses a four-node KRaft-mode cluster deployed on-premise. We validate the design through a 36-configuration benchmarking campaign that sweeps partition counts, replication factors, and client concurrency levels. Results show that throughput scales primarily with concurrent producers, reaching a peak configuration average of 10.2~MB/s, while end-to-end latency remains bounded at approximately 1.09~s regardless of partition count or replication factor.

Items.Authors: Paul A. Horton, Christian J. Thompson, Christopher Groppi, Jose V. Siles, Jonathan H. Kawamura
Items.Title: A modular and distributed readout, control, and on-board novelty detection architecture for ASTHROS using RabbitMQ
Items.Abstract: ASTHROS, the Astrophysics Stratospheric Telescope for High Spectral Resolution Observations at Submillimeter-wavelengths, is a balloon-borne spectrometer on a 2.5-meter antenna designed to map gas and dust in star-forming regions of the Milky Way. Its readout and control system is implemented as a distributed network of subsystems interconnected through RabbitMQ (RMQ), which serves as the payload messaging backbone. This architecture is enabled by rmqtools, an open-source Python library that standardizes subsystem integration and simplifies command, telemetry, and analysis pipelines. Beyond transport and control, rmqtools enables on-board real-time science analysis and novelty detection, allowing high-rate spectrometer data streams to be monitored in flight for anomalous spectra under limited downlink bandwidth. This work describes the development of rmqtools and the end-to-end ASTHROS system architecture supporting distributed control, telemetry, data storage, and analysis.

Items.Authors: Rin Yamada, Fumika Demachi, Takuto Ito, Atsushi Nishimura, Yosuke Shibata, Masahiro Kato, Toshikazu Onishi, Takeru Matsumoto, Yuito Okamoto, Kota Tada, Yamato Matsuzuki, Tatsumi Ishikawa, Fuuna Takayama, Ryo Nakagawa, Kaoru Nishikawa, Hidetoshi Sano, Kengo Tachihara
Items.Title: A new telescope controlling system based on python/ROS2
Items.Abstract: We have developed a telescope, frontend, and backend control system based on the Robot Operating System (ROS) 2, and implemented it on the NANTEN2 telescope, the OMU 1.85-m telescope, and several laboratory measurement systems. The key feature of this system is its high configurational flexibility, achieved through a distributed architecture in which the entire system is composed of multiple computers and network devices. Each node communicates via TCP or UDP protocols, which are abstracted through ROS packages. The antenna driving accuracy achieved with this system is better than a few arcseconds for both NANTEN2 and the OMU 1.85-m telescope, fully satisfying their scientific requirements. NANTEN2 is equipped with the 20-IF NASCO receiver, and we confirmed that the 16-board XFFTS spectrometer system—with 32,768 channels per board—can be recorded without data loss. In the presentation, we will also show results from the test observations.

Items.Authors: G. Lombardi, O. Cuevas Ahumada
Items.Title: A probabilistic seeing-forecast system for the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias: methodology, validation, and operational integration
Items.Abstract: We present a probabilistic seeing forecast system developed for the 10.4m Gran Telescopio Canarias (GTC) to support dynamic operations. The model combines numerical weather prediction, empirical calibration of turbulence strength, and a machine-learning post-processing layer (MOS) trained on TNG DIMM and GTC meteorological data. In addition to predicting deterministic values, the system provides probability distributions over discrete seeing intervals with hourly resolution up to 48 hours ahead, enabling direct application to queue scheduling and AO planning. The physical component applies wind-dependent calibrations, while the MOS layer corrects residual systematic errors using local meteorological features. Validation is performed through a back-casting framework on two years of data. The final model achieves a median absolute error of 0.16" and RMSE of 0.33". The system is currently integrated into the GTC operations, while nowcasting features are under development.

Items.Authors: Geart van der Ploeg
Items.Title: A sub-arcsecond, ultra-low-SWaP star tracker for small satellite attitude determination
Items.Abstract: This work presents a compact, ultra-low-SWaP star tracker achieving sub-arcsecond attitude determination. The system is validated using on-sky data from a 40 mm aperture optical assembly, and is expected to achieve an accuracy better than 1″ in LEO and ~0.2″ in GEO. The tracker derives absolute pointing (RA, Dec, and field rotation) by detecting stellar sources, constructing asterisms, and matching them in real time to a reference catalog. It supports both first-fix operation without prior knowledge and fast continuous tracking using previous solutions as priors. Performance is assessed across dense and sparse fields, the galactic plane, and regions significantly affected by dust extinction. Operational factors for LEO, including daylight-side background and Sun-avoidance constraints, are evaluated. Results show that high-accuracy attitude determination is achievable with unprecedentedly low SWaP, providing a strong sensor input for autonomous pointing control in future missions.

Items.Authors: Monde Manzini
Items.Title: A systems engineering approach to implementing and characterizing PTP for the SKA-mid telescope
Items.Abstract: This paper details the systems engineering approach for implementing the interim White Rabbit-based PTP (WRPTP) timing standard in the SKA-Mid telescope, crucial for detecting nanohertz gravitational waves via pulsar timing. Verified in the Integration and Test Facility (ITF), an IEEE 1588-compliant chain of Grandmaster, boundary/transparent clocks, and end-nodes achieved <200 ns principal-assistant offsets and <200 ps stability—meeting stringent dish control requirements for millisecond pulsar tracking. Results validate WRPTP’s performance, address fibre calibration effects, and compare it with the planned GNSS-based final standard, informing SKA-Mid's long-term timing distribution strategy.

Items.Authors: Christoph Braig, Peter Predehl
Items.Title: A tunable x-ray telescope with ultrahigh angular resolution
Items.Abstract: We analyze separated lens doublets for X-ray astronomy at an angular resolution of one milli-arcsec or less in the energy range (6 − 14) keV. Based on the blazed Fresnel lens (FL) and a refractive corrector, such arrangements can be tuned over several keV from the 2nd to the 3rd focal length dispersion order, by adjusting the lens-to-lens distance of ~ 10² km. By means of the matrix formalism, the optical properties like focal spot size, depth of field and bandpass are derived as a function of the observed photon energy. The tuning range can be extended using multiple diffraction orders and the properties of the FL. As an example, a design for the Fe K alpha line (6.4 keV) is specified. By simulations, the transverse chromatic aberration is estimated for off-axis objects. Optimized versions with segmented and compact lenses are evaluated and compared in terms of their performance. Potential next generation space telescopes of this type operate in formation flight over ~ 10³ km.

Items.Authors: That Chomchuen, Krittapas Chanchaiworawit, Pakawat Prasit, Kantapong Tharawan, Thansita Thomrungpiyathan, Jitsupa Paenoi, Pathompong Butpan, Rungrit Anutarawiramkul, Anuphong Inpan, Suchinno Kanthum, Manlika Pinkaew, Apichat Leckngam
Items.Title: A unified software architecture for real-time autoguiding and robotization of low-resolution spectrographs at TRT and TNT
Items.Abstract: At the Thai National Observatory, LRS observations on the 2.4-m Thai National Telescope previously required separate manual tools for ZWO guiding, Andor acquisition, plate solving, and drift measurement. We develop a unified, modular software stack that merges these functions to enable low-latency, closed-loop autoguiding and robotic spectrograph operation. The system provides a hardware-abstraction layer for ZWO/Andor SDKs, performs one-time plate solving on a reference frame to obtain RA, Dec, and PA, tracks guide stars, and matches each 3-frame bundle to estimate translational/rotational offsets. Corrections are sent via API to the telescope mount and supervised by a state machine that triggers Andor science exposures once guiding stabilizes. The same architecture supports full automation for ColoRS in the TRT network.

Items.Authors: Frédérique Baron, Jonathan Saint-Antoine, Lison Malo, Philippe Vallée, Étienne Artigau, René Doyon
Items.Title: A user perspective on the transition from ASIC to NGCII electronics in ESO's ELT environment
Items.Abstract: We present our approach to integrating three Teledyne H4RG detectors for the YJH arm of the ANDES spectrograph on ESO's Extremely Large Telescope, with particular focus on the transition from Application Specific Integrated Circuit (ASIC)-based to NGCII-based control electronics required for the ELT environment. This work builds on our successful implementation of H4RG detectors for NIRPS at ESO's 3.6m telescope in La Silla (Bouchy et al., 2025), which utilised Teledyne's multipurpose ASIC control and interface electronics (MACIE) in the VLT environment. This provides a direct comparison as we now adopt ESO's NGCII detector controllers mandated for ANDES in the ELT environment.

Items.Authors: Piero D'Incecco, Mauro Dolci, Gianluca Di Rico, Aleksei Martynov, Gaetano Di Achille, Philippa J. Mason, Gerard Gallardo i Peres, James B. Garvin, Justin R. Filiberto, Elizabeth B. Rampe, Sriram S. Bhiravarasu, Tibor Kremic, Dmitry A. Gorinov, Stefano Branca, Rosa Anna Corsaro, Carmelo Monaco, Ivan Lopez, Pier Raffaele Platania, Goro Komatsu, Giuseppe Salerno, Edoardo Spezzati, Domenico Tescione, Alessandra Ciappa, Clive Oppenheimer, Stefano Di Frischia, Gaetano Valentini, Matteo Canzari
Items.Title: A Venus in-situ reference mission concept within the CONVERGE network
Items.Abstract: CONVERGE (COordinated Network for Venus and Exoplanet Research and GEoscience) is a lightweight international network linking Venus exploration, planetary geoscience, terrestrial analogues, laboratory measurements, and rocky-exoplanet studies. Within this framework, we present a Venus in-situ reference mission concept designed to obtain surface ground truth still missing from the current Venus exploration campaign. The concept combines an orbiter/relay element, a short-lived analytical lander, and a longer-lived passive seismic/environmental node targeting a young volcanic rise such as Imdr Regio. The landed payload would measure mineralogy and bulk chemistry through compact XRD/XRF instrumentation, provide local imaging and atmospheric context, and monitor ground motion. These co-located measurements would anchor orbital and atmospheric observations and support rocky-exoplanet interpretation.

Items.Authors: A. Tan, P. Ashworth, P. S. Barry, C. S. Benson, K. Dibert, H. Gordon-Moys, K. S. Karkare, I. Morris
Items.Title: A waveguide spectrometer for high-resolution millimeter-wave imaging
Items.Abstract: We present the design and development of a novel, compact integrated spectrometer-on-a-chip operating at millimeter (mm) and submillimeter (sub-mm) wavelengths. SWISS, the Superconducting Waveguide Integrated Submillimeter Spectrometer, promises to significantly improve on spectral resolution, optical efficiency, and frequency coverage over current mm-wave spectrometers using a free-space rectangular waveguide architecture.

Items.Authors: Diego Paredes-Sanz, Sonny Massahi, Sara Svendsen, Desirée Della Monica Ferreira, Michael Avngaard, Finn Erland Christensen, Arne S. Jegers, Alessandro Morello, Andreas E. Nielsen, Mia J. Krag, Mads H. Jensen
Items.Title: Achieving W/SiC multilayers with 1nm d-spacing and graded mirror coatings up to 550mm following upgrades to the DTU475 coating chamber
Items.Abstract: We present upgrades and expanded capabilities of the DTU475 DC magnetron sputtering chamber at the Technical University of Denmark. The system, previously used for the production of NuSTAR multilayer optics, has been refurbished to improve deposition throughput, process stability, and coating uniformity.   The upgraded chamber enables uniform coating of substrates up to 550 mm in length, extending its applicability to large X-ray optical elements for synchrotron beamlines and calibration facilities. We demonstrate the deposition of periodic SiC/W multilayers with d-spacings down to 1 nm and interface roughness of 0.3 nm. In addition, we show the capability to produce three-dimensionally graded coatings with controlled thickness gradients along the axial, lateral, and depth directions of the mirror. These results establish DTU475 as a versatile platform for advanced X-ray optics development.

Items.Title: Advanced time-division multiplexed readout chain for the BICEP array 90/150 GHz receiver
Items.Abstract: This work presents the performance of the advanced time-division multiplexed (TDM) readout chain for the BICEP Array 90/150 GHz receiver. BA4-90/150, deploying to the South Pole in 2026–27, will use photon-noise limited, feedhorn-coupled TES detectors and an upgraded DC SQUID based TDM system. Improvements include faster, fully differential SQUID designs, higher TES signal amplification, and hierarchical row-addressing that reduces wiring required for row switching by 25%. New warm electronics provide fully differential circuits and higher bandwidth, reducing RF susceptibility and aliased noise contributions. On-sky demonstration in BA4 will establish a new low-noise, high-bandwidth TDM architecture for future CMB observatories.

Items.Authors: Srikanth Panini Singam, Stephen Bongiorno, Danielle Gurgew
Items.Title: Advancements in Segmented Replicated X-ray Optics (SRXO)
Items.Abstract: Segmented Replicated X-ray Optics (SRXO) offers a promising pathway for next-generation flagship X-ray missions, enabling large collecting areas with sub-arcsecond angular resolution. We present recent advances in SRXO development at NASA Marshall Space Flight Center, including: (1) optimized electroforming processes that significantly improve thickness uniformity and reduce stress variation across segments, resulting in enhanced optical performance; (2) novel stress compensation techniques introducing customized local stress fields tailored to individual segment metrology for systematic figure error correction; and (3) investigation of alternative alloy compositions including high-cobalt NiCo and NiCoP formulations that demonstrate improved hardness and dimensional stability. These advances establish SRXO as a viable solution for future flagship X-ray astronomy missions requiring both large effective area and exceptional angular resolution.

Items.Authors: Uriel Conod, Jacob Taylor
Items.Title: Advances in pyTomoAO: new tomographic and SLODAR capabilities for Multi-Guide-Star AO Systems
Items.Abstract: Adaptive optics (AO) systems require robust tomographic reconstruction and accurate turbulence profiling to achieve high-performance correction on large field of view. pyTomoAO is an open-source Python framework designed to compute tomographic reconstructor, support algorithm development, simulation, and diagnostics for AO systems. This paper discusses the latest developments in pyTomoAO, including a newly integrated SLODAR module optimized for multi–laser guide star configurations. The module enables efficient computation of Shack–Hartmann slope correlations and retrieval of vertical turbulence profiles with configurable layer geometry. These new tools allow performance validation, and real-time diagnostics, with applications to tomographic (multi-object, and wide-field) AO systems. The updated capabilities further establish pyTomoAO as a flexible platform for AO system design and analysis on current 8–10 m telescopes and future ELTs.

Items.Authors: Vincent Affatato, Sander Blommaert, Luc Boucher, Frédéric Lemmel, Jean Le Graët, Eloy Hernandez, Malik Mansour, Thibaut Prod'Homme, Conor Robinson, Erik Ryman, Peter Verhoeve
Items.Title: Advancing detector technology: ESA's functional characterisation of four 2k×2k LmAPD MCT arrays for space science missions
Items.Abstract: In the framework of ESA’s Voyage 2050 programme, the Payload Validation Section (SCI-FIV) supports the development of next-generation Mercury Cadmium Telluride (MCT) Linear-mode Avalanche Photodiode (LmAPD) large arrays, a key technology for future space telescopes targeting high-precision galactic astrometry. As part of this effort, SCI-FIV has collaborated on the IBEX detector, manufactured by Leonardo UK: a 2k × 2k MCT array operating at 80 K and optimised for the 800–2500 nm range. The device features a radiation-hard readout integrated circuit (ROIC) and aims to deliver low dark current, sub-electron read noise and therefore single photon sensitivity, and high quantum efficiency in the near-infrared. Over the past year, four IBEX devices were characterised through an extensive cryogenic test campaign. This work presents the test setup, main technical challenges, and key results, highlighting lessons learned from assessing this novel detector technology.

Items.Authors: Ryan Dungee, Suresh Sivanandam, Mark Chun, Mark Barnet, Shaojie Chen, Saugata Dutt, Gavin Hay, Ting Li, Matteo Statti, Robin Swanson
Items.Title: Ae’o: a SCIDAR instrument for Maunakea
Items.Abstract: We are currently developing a Stereo-SCIDAR instrument that we have named Ae’o, which is destined for the University of Hawaii 2.2-meter telescope on Maunakea. Here, we present the optical design and progress on testing and assembly of the instrument. Additionally, we cover the software being developed to run the instrument in an autonomous manner. In particular we cover the observing strategy, collecting turbulence profiles ~2-3 times per night, and automated data reduction to make these profiles publicly available as soon as possible after observation. Finally, we will also discuss the machine learning approaches that are being explored as a means of improving the accuracy of the SCIDAR measurements under a range of different turbulence conditions, as well as the possibility of increasing the vertical resolution of our profiles.

Items.Authors: Liyue Tong, Jiaben Lin, Mingfu Shao, Hui Wang
Items.Title: AI4S Telescope: a multi-agent embodied intelligence system for hypothesis-driven astronomical observation
Items.Abstract: The AI4S Telescope presents a multi-agent embodied intelligence system for autonomous astronomical observation. Three specialized agents—Scientist, Observer, and Engineer—collaborate to transform scientific questions into validated hypotheses, executable observation plans, and adaptive control algorithms. The Scientist generates and filters hypotheses through simulation-based validation; the Observer dynamically schedules and executes observations; the Engineer evolves control strategies. Demonstrated in solar flare prediction, the system significantly enhances scientific output per observing hour while maintaining robust adaptability. This work bridges AI-driven scientific reasoning with physical telescope operations, establishing a new paradigm for autonomous astronomical discovery through intelligent software infrastructure.

Items.Title: AIT of the phasing diagnostic station (PDS) of the ELT: strategy and first results
Items.Abstract: The Phasing Diagnostic Station (PDS) of the ELT is a commissioning instrument that will receive the first photons collected from the telescope. It has a modular approach. Each module refer to a subsystem with a defined function, has defined entrance/exit pupil and focal planes, can be aligned, integrated and tested against requirements independently and has a clear opto-mechanical interface. Here we will describe the AIT strategy and tools, report the status of the alignment and show some of the initial results from the tested subsystems.

Items.Authors: Yu Chieh Huang, Remko Stuik, Dirk Lesman, Shiang-Yu Wang, Ioannis Politopoulos, Felix Bettonvil, Bernhard R. Brandl, Chad Salo
Items.Title: AIT support equipment design for METIS
Items.Abstract: The Mid-Infrared E-ELT Imager and Spectrometer (METIS) for the Extremely Large Telescope in Chile, is expecting to begin the system-level Assembly, Integration, and Testing (AIT) at Leiden University in 2026. To support this phase, the Academia Sinica Institute of Astronomy and Astrophysics (ASIAA) has developed dedicated Support Equipment (SEQ), including the AIT Support Frame (ASF), ASF transportation container, clean booth, and AIT Lifting Platform (ALP). This paper presents the key design considerations, engineering analyses, and final implementation of these SEQ units for enabling the precise and reliable integration of METIS subsystems.

Items.Authors: Leo Nelson, Alex Haughton, Brian Fleming
Items.Title: Alignment of a far ultraviolet grating array using the laser cube
Items.Abstract: The INtegral Field Ultraviolet Spectroscopic Experiment (INFUSE) sounding rocket payload, developed by the Colorado Ultraviolet Spectroscopy Program (CUSP), is the first far-UV integral field spectrograph launched into space. The INFUSE payload uses a 26-element image slicer to create 26 long-slit images across the entire field. INFUSE's first launch in October 2023 returned valuable science, but the data returned required extra decoding and deparsing as many of the resultant spectra fell outside their designated detector spaces and, in some cases, overlapped on top of each other. To reduce the danger to the detector during the lengthy realignment procedures, we devised a novel method for separating the grating array from the payload entirely during readjustment. Using a commercially available 1.5W Wicked Lasers LaserCube, we replicated geometrically similar conditions to those inside the payload, limiting contamination of the detector, and allowing easier access for corrections.

Items.Authors: Juan Larrain, Rodrigo Brito, Thomas Abbott
Items.Title: An AI-class data center for ALMA Observatory upgrades
Items.Abstract: Systems engineering and project management approach to the design and construction of an AI class data center for the ALMA radio telescope in northern Chile. The new facility will house the next-generation correlator, supplying it with electrical power, cooling water, and conditioned air. Globally distributed stakeholders and an operating observatory at an elevation of 2950 m add to the complexity of the project.

Items.Authors: Murdock Hart
Items.Title: An assessment of reflectance measurements performed at the Large Binocular Telescope
Items.Abstract: Bare aluminum is used for reflective optics in astronomy because it has a high reflectance from the near-ultraviolet to the infrared, but these surfaces are continuously degrading due to oxidation and other environmental factors. In situ reflectivity measurements are the primary method of assessing the condition of bare aluminum reflective surfaces at ground based astronomical observatories. Through a regular cadence of reflectance measurements, the degradation of these surfaces can be quantified and monitored to determine their impact upon throughput.    The Large Binocular Telescope (LBT) has used an OPO CT7a for reflectance measurements since January 2020. A recent aggregation of these measurements highlighted numerous outliers, and questionable absolute reflectance values. We undertook this analysis to better understand these measurements, and to ultimately have a robust metric by which to determine when the LBT's bare aluminum optics require realuminization.

Items.Authors: Manjunath Bestha, Sivarani Thirupathi, Athira Unni, Parvathy Menon, Devika Divakar
Items.Title: An observational study of systematics affecting low-resolution multiobject transmission spectroscopy using HFOSC-HCT
Items.Abstract: Ground-based multi-object low-resolution transmission spectroscopy (Mo-LRTS) is a commonly used method to study exoplanet atmospheres. However, these observations are affected by several time-variable systematics, such as differential slit losses, color-dependent seeing, guiding jitter, and variations in atmospheric transparency, as well as instrumental effects like wavelength drift, flexure, and trace instability. Using HFOSC-HCT data, we investigate how these effects influence the extracted light curves and transmission spectra. Differential shifts between the program and reference stars can create or hide apparent transit features, while small wavelength misalignments can bias low-resolution spectra. We explore mitigation strategies, improved extraction methods, and common-mode corrections. This work demonstrates that modeling and correcting systematics are crucial for obtaining reliable exoplanet atmosphere measurements from ground-based Mo-LRTS using HFOSC.

Items.Authors: Thomas R. Swindle, Erik Small, Zach Gazak, Justin Fletcher
Items.Title: An open-source observatory control application for space domain awareness and time-domain astronomy
Items.Abstract: SensorKit is an autonomous observatory control system designed for satellite tracking and follow-up of rapid astronomical transients. A high-level agent built on NATS JetStream coordinates tasking, scheduling, hardware control, data processing, and other services for distributed, low-latency operation across potentially volatile environments. By default, SensorKit communicates with leading device platforms including Alpaca, INDIGO, NINA, the Observable Space Node Platform and PWI4, and TheSky, with others added via plugin support. It executes tasks based on safety, weather, viewing geometry, and user-defined constraints and provides microservices for astrometry/photometry, cloud detection, and autofocus, extendable to other standard observatory routines. Its central `program` layer supports communication with the Unified Data Library for space domain awareness and provides an API for custom tasking or data-delivery pipelines. All software is open-source and hosted on GitHub and PyPi.

Items.Authors: Shao Qi
Items.Title: An Open-Source, Cross-Platform Architecture for Autonomous Observatory Control: A Native Alpaca Implementation with an Integrated ASCOM-COM Bridge
Items.Abstract: The transition to modern, cross-platform observatory control is hindered by the prevalence of the Windows-only ASCOM COM architecture. We present a novel, open-source control system designed to bridge this gap. Our architecture features a native ASCOM Alpaca implementation in Python, enabling true OS independence. Its core innovation is an integrated, bi-directional ASCOM-COM-to-Alpaca bridge, providing seamless backward compatibility with the vast ecosystem of legacy devices. This work offers a powerful sequencing engine and an architectural blueprint that solves the protocol adoption challenge, enabling flexible, network-native, and autonomous control for the wider astronomical community.

Items.Authors: Yigit Dallilar, Vipin Kumar, Michael Wiest, Lucas Labadie, Adhirath Deshmukh, Margo Gassmueller, Roy van Boekel, Emilie Bouzerand, Wolfgang Brandner, Dennis Dolkens, Adrian Glauser, Sander Kwast, Dirk Lesman, Mirka Maresca, Wim Pessemier, Gert Raskin, Christian Straubmeier, Remko Stuik, Niels Tromp, Felix Bettonvil, Bernhard Brandl
Items.Title: An overview of the as-built subassemblies and components of WCU subsystem of METIS with a focus on the full subsystem integration
Items.Abstract: Following the finalization of its subassemblies and the full subsystem integration starting in 2026, we provide an overlook to the finalized subassemblies of the WCU subsystem of METIS and the full subsystem integration efforts along with the lessons learned therein. The as-built status and features of its core components will be discussed. This is complemented with the further discussion on the subsystem integration activities along with support equipment facilitating the integration and handling of the WCU and its components and the final performance of the WCU.

Items.Title: An overview of the stray light findings and interpretation during the on-sky commissioning of LSSTCam
Items.Abstract: Wide-field telescopes such as the Vera C. Rubin are intrinsically difficult to shield from some unwanted stray and scattered light. The paper distills the experience of the Rubin commissioning for what concerns the stray light investigations, modeling, and mitigation in a wide system perspective embracing optical design, engineering, and commissioning aspects of the newest, large ground-based facility for astronomy.

Items.Authors: Elisa Radjabou, Damien Prêle, Manuel Gonzalez, Michel Piat, Shawn Henderson, Brianna Cantrall
Items.Title: Analytical modelling of TES noise: transfer functions across the superconducting transition
Items.Abstract: This work addresses the critical need to characterize detector noise for future cosmology experiments focused on measuring the B-mode signal of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB). Like many CMB observatories, the model is based on Transition-Edge Sensors (TES) and SQUID-based Time-Domain Multiplexing (TDM) readout technology.  We present a new formalism developing transfer functions for phonon, TES, and shunt resistance current noises, clearly showing their characteristic frequencies. This formulation enables the prediction of total and individual noise shapes, comparison with measurements, and direct calculation of key parameters such as cut-off frequencies and maximum amplitude spectral density values. The superconducting to normal transition is modeled to be fed into the noise model. The analysis also examines how current noise amplitude model and measurements behave at various working points within the superconducting transition.

Items.Authors: Christophe Giordano, Aziz Ziad, Alessandro Aresta, Eric Aristidi, Christophe Bailet, Chiara Bertolin, Marcel Carbillet, Yan Caujolle, Stefano Cavazzani, Clémence Edouard, Yenny Gonzalez-Ramos, Abdanour Irbah, Arnaud Le Kernec, Olivier Liandrat, Nicolas Pascal, Alvaro-Jose Pascual-Garcia, Jérôme Riedi, Nicolas Schmutz, Stéphane Victori, Mary Joe Medlej
Items.Title: ANAtOLIA: from first light to multi-site atmospheric characterization
Items.Abstract: Atmospheric turbulence, clouds, and aerosols limit astronomical observations and the availability of optical ground stations. The ANAtOLIA project, funded by ESA, was developed to address these limitations by providing an autonomous atmospheric monitoring station. The ANAtOLIA station combines three complementary instruments: the GMT turbulence monitor, the Sky Insight all-sky camera for clouds measurements, and the Cimel CE318-T photometer for aerosols characterization. Since 2023, four stations have been deployed at four European sites (Calern, Cebreros, Catania, and Sintra) to perform a 2-year measurement campaign. This paper presents an overview of ANAtOLIA station, its operation, and the statistical results obtained across the four sites, including inter-comparisons in terms of turbulence, clouds and aerosols. The ANAtOLIA station demonstrated its efficiency as a high-performance platform for site qualification and the optimization of optical links and astronomical observations.

Items.Authors: Lorenzo Cabona, Marcello Scalera, Alessio Zanutta, Matteo De Magistris, Igor Coretti, Chiara Selmi, Matteo Aliverti, Edoardo Redaelli, Ernesto Oliva, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessandro Marconi
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: MBSE-based interface management
Items.Abstract: Clear identification and management of interfaces are key to the success of complex systems like ANDES Spectrograph. This contribution presents the methodological approach adopted by the ANDES System Team to ensure technical consistency, completeness, and traceability throughout the system development lifecycle. Interface management encompasses both internal and external interfaces. The Model-Based Interface Management approach implemented for ANDES ensures robust configuration control, full synchronization between interface definitions and the system architecture, and complete bidirectional traceability across all levels of the system hierarchy. Interfaces are represented within a structured hierarchy of Interfaces, Interface Channels, and Interface Ends, capturing the logical and physical interaction points between subsystems. The ANDES methodology shows how an MBSE-driven interface framework improves consistency, traceability, and verification in complex instrument development.

Items.Authors: Chiara Selmi, Alessio Zanutta, Marcello Agostino Scalera, Edoardo Maria Alberto Redaelli, Giorgio Pariani, Matteo Aliverti, Igor Coretti, Marco Landoni, Marco Riva, Ernesto Oliva, Lorenzo Cabona, Enrico Giro, Paolo Di Marcantonio, Alessandro Marconi
Items.Title: ANDES, the high resolution spectrograph for the ELT: optimization of system requirements management in view of the preliminary design review
Items.Abstract: This work outlines the optimized System Requirements Management methodology implemented for the ANDES Project as it approaches its Preliminary Design Review (PDR) in 2026. Requirements are formally tracked and maintained using Cameo Systems Modeler, applying an MBSE framework to guarantee structural integrity and robust design element interconnection. Dynamic collaboration with subsystem teams is facilitated through the combined use of Confluence and JIRA, streamlining communication, task assignment, and formal requirement acceptance. We detail the solutions that enabled ANDES to achieve the necessary technical maturity through this streamlined workflow.
